post.description:
Atomically transitions a server to the terminal `Disabled` state: cancels
any in-flight auto-reconnect supervisor, bumps generation, tears down the
live transport, clears the tool catalog, and writes `Disabled`. The
server's synthetic tools are removed from the tool registry and
`McpServerDisabled` is emitted via the SSE event stream.

200.description: Disabled (or was already disabled — idempotent). McpServerDisabled event emitted on transition.

401.description: Authentication required: request must include a valid `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header matching the daemon's startup credential.

post.description:
Synchronously shuts down the named MCP server's live transport, marks the
handle as `Disconnected`, and emits `McpServerDisconnected` via the SSE
event stream.

Status codes:
- 200 — server was `Connected`: transport shut down, event emitted.
- 200 — server was already `Disconnected` or `Reconnecting`: no-op, no event.
- 404 — `server_name` not in current config.
- 500 — server is in config but has no registry handle (internal invariant violation).

**Does not** spawn an `auto_reconnect_loop` — the handle is left idle until
the caller issues a subsequent `POST /mcp/{server_name}/reconnect`.

post.description:
Clears a `Disabled` server and attempts a fresh reconnect. If the server
is already `Connected`, returns 200 as a no-op. Otherwise dispatches a
fire-and-forget reconnect with a supervisor. The outcome streams via
`DaemonEvent::McpServerConnected` or `DaemonEvent::McpServerDisabled`.

AdventurousHandoffResponse.description:
Body returned by `GET /adventurous-handoff` and successful
`POST /adventurous-handoff` requests.

`enabled` reflects the raw session-scoped flag. The computed
`adventurous_handoff_active` on `SessionStateSnapshot` ANDs this with
whether the active facet exposes `handoff_plan`.

AgentsMdEntry.description:
A discovered `AGENTS.md` file that should be re-attached after
compaction so facet/project context remains live.

AskUserQuestionPayload.description: Structured payload for a model-originated user-question prompt.

AskUserQuestionReply.description: Minimal HTTP response payload posted by a client for one question.

AvailableModelEntry.description:
One entry in the daemon's available-model list, carried in
`SessionStateSnapshot.available_models` so the TUI can populate its
`@model:` typeahead from the daemon's resolved config (including dynamic
provider models) rather than from a client-side config snapshot.

reasoning.description: Reasoning capability metadata for this model.

oneOf.description:
Opaque signature for an Anthropic thinking block. Anthropic
emits this as a separate `content_block_delta` event with delta
type `signature_delta` near the end of the thinking block. There
is exactly one per thinking block; `finalize_blocks` takes the
last observed value. Preserve verbatim — do not derive, truncate,
or summarize. (TD-2 contract.)

id.description:
Upstream-minted reasoning item id (always `rs_`-prefixed).
See `ContentBlock::OpenAiReasoningOpaque::id` for why we
propagate it through every delta rather than regenerating.

oneOf.description:
Readable summary text from a `reasoning_summary_text.delta`
event for an opaque reasoning block. The OpenAI Responses API
sends these alongside the encrypted-content deltas; routing them
into this separate variant keeps display text isolated from the
encrypted blob, preventing replay corruption.

BlockDeltaPayload.description:
An incremental update to a content block, emitted by
`ContentBlockDelta`.

For text-like blocks the payload carries the new bytes; for
`tool_use` it carries partial JSON (the provider streams tool input
as unvalidated chunks). `SignatureDelta` is a distinct variant
carrying the opaque Anthropic signature for a thinking block; it
arrives as a separate `content_block_delta` event with delta type
`signature_delta` and must be preserved verbatim for turn-2 replay.

CacheMissAlert.description:
Fired when a provider turn completes with a complete prompt-cache miss
(zero cached tokens) on a large context. Carries the occupancy token
count for display.

occupancy_tokens.description:
Total token occupancy that was fully reprocessed because the prompt
cache served zero cached tokens.

Capability.description:
Capability declared by an extension manifest. Surfaces in
`ExtensionContext.capabilities` to drive the Capability interrogative
flow; the runtime semantics live in Layer 6.

`Ord` / `PartialOrd` are derived so the approval-record canonicaliser
in `polytoken-extensions::approval` has a stable sort key that does
not depend on `Debug` formatting. Derive ordering is declaration
order; that becomes the canonical ordering for `approved_capabilities`
on disk.

ClarificationOption.description: A selectable response option for a clarification interrogative.

ClassifierOutcome.description:
Classifier decision outcome emitted after an autonomous monitor evaluates
a tool call.

CompactAccepted.description:
Body of the 202 Accepted response from `POST /compact`.

The daemon mints a fresh `CompactionId` when the compaction pass is
accepted and returns it immediately; the pass itself proceeds
asynchronously and its lifecycle events stream via `/events`.

CompactionId.description: Identifier for a single compaction operation within a session.

CompactionProjection.description:
Typed, persisted projection metadata for the compaction continuation prompt.
Stored alongside the `continuation_prompt` string so subsequent compactions
can rebuild the earlier spine deterministically without reparsing the
rendered canonical prompt.

compaction_epoch.description:
Monotonic compaction epoch. The first new-code compaction assigns 0;
each subsequent successful compaction increments by 1.

version.description:
Forward-compat version gate. Starts at 1 for projections created by
the new code. Legacy fenceposts lacking this field default to 0,
signaling "no prior projection".

id.description:
Upstream-minted identifier (always `rs_`-prefixed). The
OpenAI Responses API ties an encrypted-content blob to
the exact id it issued on the producing turn; replaying a
reasoning item on a follow-up turn requires echoing that
id verbatim — a freshly-generated id produces
`invalid_encrypted_content`. We therefore carry the id on
the block type rather than synthesize one at serialize
time.

summary.description:
Readable summary text extracted from
`reasoning_summary_text.delta` events that the API sends
alongside the encrypted blob. This is display-only content;
it is never serialized into the outbound replay request (the
wire always sends an empty `summary` array). Old history
without this field deserializes with an empty string.

ContentBlock.description: A fully-formed content block emitted during a turn.

ContentBlockKind.description:
The kind-label of a content block — the discriminator emitted by
`ContentBlockStart` before any delta bytes flow. Tagged with
`#[serde(tag = "type")]` so all variants serialize as objects
(`{"type":"text"}`, `{"type":"tool_use","id":"...","name":"..."}`).
`ToolUse` carries `id`, `name`, and optional opaque provider metadata so that `finalize_blocks` can
reconstruct a fully-formed `ContentBlock::ToolUse` without empty
strings. All other variants are unit variants and produce `{"type":"<name>"}`.

ContextUsageSnapshot.description:
Stable completed-context gauge for status/UI consumers. Reflects the
context footprint after the most recent completed turn or lifecycle
operation (rewind, clear, compaction, model/facet switch). When the
provider reports usage telemetry, the gauge uses it; when telemetry is
unavailable, it falls back to a history-based estimate. Omitted from
`SessionStateSnapshot` when no context exists yet.

limit_tokens.description: Total context window for the active model.

used_tokens.description:
Tokens counted from the stable completed-context gauge. When
provider usage telemetry is unavailable, this is a history-based
estimate of the current context footprint.

CurrentGoal.description:
The snapshot object for the active goal of a session.

Every field is stable public surface. Optional timestamp and terminal-reason
fields are omitted from the wire when absent. A cleared goal is the absence
of a current goal (a `None` value), not a distinct lifecycle state.

activated_at.description: When the goal most recently became active.

blocked_at.description: When the goal most recently became blocked, if it has.

completed_at.description: When the goal reached a completed state, if it has.

continuation_count.description: Number of times the session has continued this goal across resumptions.

created_at.description: When the goal was first created.

last_reiterated_at.description:
When the goal summary was last reiterated into the active context, if it
has been.

source.description: How the goal came to be the active goal.

summary.description: Short, human-readable summary of the goal.

oneOf.description: Why the goal reached a terminal state, if it has.

updated_at.description: When the goal was last updated.

oneOf.description: Liveness tick. `session_id` lives on the envelope.

A new content block is about to stream. The `kind` narrows the
shape of the deltas that will follow.

An incremental update to an in-flight content block. The `delta`
payload is tagged with its own `type` discriminator inside the
outer envelope (see `BlockDeltaPayload`).

The in-flight content block is complete. No more deltas will
arrive for this `block_index`.
The assistant turn has begun; content block events will follow.
The assistant turn is complete.
The provider reported an error attributable to this prompt.

Subscriber-synthesized: events were dropped between the last
delivered frame and this one. Carries `Envelope::seq = None`.

Snapshot invalidation for fields returned by `GET /state`.

The payload is an invalidation signal only. Clients that care about
affected domains should fetch `GET /state`; the full todo/flag/env
state is intentionally not duplicated in SSE.

Emitted when the operator-visible session title changes. `source`
distinguishes an automatic inference from an operator `/title` change
so clients can surface the former with a one-time hint.

Emitted on successful runtime model swap via `POST /model`.
Surfaces the new active model to clients without exposing the
underlying `ModelConfig`.

Emitted when the active runtime permission monitor changes after
startup, such as via `POST /permission-monitor` or reload.

additional_context.description:
Hook-provided context or reason text for live display. Carries
`additional_context` from allow outcomes and the effective
context/reason text (including stdout fallback where applicable)
from block/deny/cancel outcomes; `None` when the hook output
has no user-visible text.

max_attempts.description:
Total attempts allowed (max_retries + 1). Lets clients display
"Compaction retry 1/3" without needing to know the config value.

oneOf.description:
A notification was enqueued for the active session. Surfaced to
subscribers immediately; delivery to the model happens on the
next `/prompt` turn (see `NotificationsDrained`).

The daemon drained `count` notifications from the per-session
queue at the start of a prompt turn, packaging them into a
single `Message::Notification` delivered to the model.

The per-session auto-drain toggle was switched. `subagent_handle`
is intentionally absent — this is a session-global toggle, never
subagent-scoped.

A daemon-owned system reminder was durably persisted. Clients may render
this optional context card when their visibility settings allow it.

Emitted once per tool-search (aggregate). Lists the tool names
revealed by a single search invocation.

Emitted when the tool-exposure plan changes. Carries the new
active loading mode and counts.

`exposed_count` is the number of tools invocable right now
(`full_schema + revealed`). `catalog_count` is the number of
tools visible in the deferred catalog but not yet invocable;
only non-zero under `NativeDeferred`.

catalog_count.description: Tools visible in the deferred catalog but not yet invocable.

oneOf.description:
Emitted when the active Goal Driver goal changes. `goal` is the current
goal after the transition, or absent when no goal is active (cleared, or
a proposal that has not been accepted). `proposed_summary` is present
only for the `proposed` and `rejected` transitions.
Emitted after an autonomous permission monitor classifies a tool call.

Emitted when an extension is successfully compiled, registered, and
published into the live `extension_registry`. Allows clients (and
integration tests) to observe readiness without polling `POST /reload`,
which has the side effect of running extension discovery again.

Also emitted by the reload-pathway `publish_extension_change_from_state`
for extensions that are newly inserted during a `POST /reload` cycle.

Emission is best-effort: if the `events_mpsc_tx` channel is full or
closed (e.g. late in shutdown), the event is dropped with a
`tracing::warn!`.

Emitted when the parent session sends a message to a running subagent
via the `message_subagent` tool. The message is delivered to the
subagent's conversation at the next agent-loop iteration boundary.
`message_preview` is truncated to 200 characters for SSE display.
TUI rendering of this event is deferred; the catch-all debug-logs it.
Emitted when an MCP server successfully connects and registers its tools.
Emitted when an MCP server connection is lost.
Emitted when the daemon is attempting to reconnect to an MCP server.

Emitted when an MCP server enters the terminal Disabled state, either
because it exhausted its reconnect attempts or was manually disabled.
A disabled server will not auto-reconnect. Use `/mcp <server> enable`
to resume connecting.
The daemon is delaying a provider stream because the provider reported usage pressure.
Present for normal prompt and subagent turns. Provider streams used by background helpers may omit it.

The daemon is retrying a provider call after a delay. This covers
both transient provider errors and provider stream idle stalls.

attempt.description:
1-indexed retry attempt number for the active retry policy. A
policy change may restart this counter even when `error_type`
stays the same.

error_summary.description: Bounded summary: error type + truncated message.

error_type.description:
Discriminator identifying the kind of error being retried. For
transient provider errors this is the serde tag of the
`ProviderError` variant (e.g. `rate_limited`, `transport`). For
provider stream idle stalls the value is `stream_idle_timeout`.

max_retries.description: Maximum retry attempts for the active retry policy.

oneOf.description:
Emitted when a tool attempts to access a path blocked by `.agentblock`
rules. Renders as a user-visible card in the conversation stream.

EarlierUserEntry.description:
An earlier-user-intent entry for the spine (chronologically ordered,
capped at 1,000 Unicode characters, followed by `assistant: [compacted]`).

EditFormatLockedResponse.description:
Body of the `POST /model` 409 response when the session edit-format lock
rejects a runtime model swap.

ErrorBody.description:
Body of any error response.

Used at Layer 0 for 503 `too_many_connections`. Future error paths add
new `code` values; clients should treat unknown codes as opaque strings.

`retry_after_seconds` is populated only for 409 `suppression_window`
responses so clients can schedule a retry without polling.

ExtensionContext.description:
Extension-level context attached to an `Interrogative` event when the
interrogative is raised by an extension load. `extension_name` and
`manifest_summary` are presentation strings; `capabilities` is the
declared capability list from the extension manifest.

retry_after_seconds.description:
Seconds the caller should wait before retrying. `i64` matches
`ProviderError::retry_after_seconds` so the type stays serde-clean
and I/O-free; negative values are semantically invalid and
producers must emit non-negative values only.

FeedbackArtifactError.description:
Error response for feedback artifact retrieval failures.
Each known error maps to a specific HTTP status code. Unrecognized errors
are preserved verbatim and use HTTP 500.

FeedbackArtifactId.description:
Opaque retrieval identifier for a feedback artifact. Scoped to the
active daemon run and the requesting client's currently attached main
session. Unguessable but confers no authorization by itself; every
retrieval reauthorizes the ID against the current run and session.

FeedbackArtifactIdentityKind.description: The source identity class of a feedback artifact snapshot. Known values (open set; other strings are forward-compatible): file.

FeedbackArtifactKind.description: The kind of feedback artifact. Known values (open set; other strings are forward-compatible): daemon_log, main_session, subagent_session.

FeedbackArtifactKindContentType.description:
Published mapping of each known feedback artifact kind to its pinned
retrieval MIME content type. Daemon log artifacts use NDJSON; session and
subagent artifacts use JSONL.

daemon_log.description:
MIME content type for daemon log artifacts on successful retrieval:
exactly `application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8`.

main_session.description:
MIME content type for main session artifacts on successful retrieval:
exactly `application/jsonl; charset=utf-8`.

subagent_session.description:
MIME content type for subagent session artifacts on successful
retrieval: exactly `application/jsonl; charset=utf-8`.

FeedbackArtifactManifest.description:
Bounded immutable snapshot catalog of feedback artifacts available for
the current daemon run and attached main session. Each entry is either
available (with an opaque retrieval ID and immutable version token) or
unavailable (with a displayable reason). The manifest exposes no
absolute paths and represents immutable snapshots, not mutable handles.

FeedbackArtifactManifestEntry.description:
One entry in the feedback artifact manifest. Each entry is either available
(with retrieval details) or unavailable (with a display reason).
Unrecognized entries are preserved verbatim so newer manifest entries
remain available to older clients.

FeedbackArtifactSnapshotMetadata.description:
Immutable identity and prefix metadata for a feedback artifact snapshot.
Published alongside the opaque version token on available manifest entries
so clients can inspect what the snapshot captured without decoding the token.

captured_length.description: Exact byte length of the prefix captured in this snapshot.

device.description: Device ID where the artifact file resided at snapshot time.

identity_kind.description: The source identity class of the artifact file, such as a regular file.

inode.description: Inode number of the artifact file at snapshot time.

prefix_digest.description: Hex-encoded digest of the captured prefix bytes.

FeedbackArtifactVersionToken.description:
Identifies an exact, immutable snapshot of a feedback artifact. Polytoken
generates this token when it catalogs the artifact; it is opaque and
clients use it only to request that specific snapshot.

FileCatalogResponse.description:
Body of `GET /files`.

Lists the project's file and directory entries that the daemon can see,
expressed as project-relative paths. Directories are marked with a trailing
`/` so they are distinguishable from files in a single list. Dotfiles and
the project's private configuration directory are always omitted. The
entries are returned in alphabetical order.

files.description: Project-relative paths, alphabetical, with a trailing `/` on directories.

GoalFileReference.description:
The markdown file a goal is persisted to, and its operator-facing display
path.

display_path.description: The operator-facing display path for the goal file.

path.description: The path the goal markdown file is persisted to.

GoalId.description:
Stable identifier for a saved-session goal.

Opaque on the wire: a plain JSON string. Two goals are equal when their
identifiers are equal.

GoalLifecycle.description: The lifecycle state of an active goal. Known values (open set; other strings are forward-compatible): active, paused, blocked, complete.

GoalLifecycleResponse.description: Body of the 200 response from `POST /goal/pause` and `POST /goal/resume`.

goal.description: The goal after the lifecycle transition.

GoalProposalActionLabels.description:
Labels for the binary approval affordance on a goal proposal. Approval is
binary (`accepted` / `rejected`), so there is an accept label and a reject
label only.

accept.description: Label for accepting the proposed goal.

reject.description: Label for rejecting the proposed goal.

GoalProposalContext.description:
Structured payload attached to a goal-proposal interrogative. The
presentation strings are carried on the event so non-TUI clients can render
the same review surface without reconstructing daemon-local state.

action_labels.description: Labels for the binary approve/reject affordance.

proposed_file_path.description: Optional proposed path for the goal markdown file.

proposed_summary.description: The proposed short summary of the goal.

GoalSetRequest.description: Body of `POST /goal` requests that create or replace the current goal.

summary.description: The short, human-readable summary of the goal.

goal.description: The newly created or replacement goal, now the active goal.

GoalSource.description: How a goal came to be the active goal. Known values (open set; other strings are forward-compatible): user, model, resumed.

GoalStatusResponse.description:
Body of the 200 response from `GET /goal`.

The current goal is absent (`None`) when no goal is set for the session.

oneOf.description:
The active goal for this session, or absent when no goal is set. A
cleared goal is represented by absence, not a distinct lifecycle state.

GoalTransition.description: The kind of change to the active goal. Known values (open set; other strings are forward-compatible): proposed, accepted, rejected, created, replaced, paused, resumed, cleared, completed, blocked, reiterated.

HealthResponse.description:
Body of `GET /health`.

Explicitly enumerates the wire fields (rather than `#[serde(flatten)]`-ing
`SessionRecord`) so that internal-only fields added to `SessionRecord`
later — e.g. auth-token hashes, owner uids — do not automatically leak
through the public HTTP surface. Use [`HealthResponse::from_session`] to
construct from a registry record.

IncludedFileEntry.description:
A file whose full (or bounded-truncated) content is re-attached after
compaction. `full_size_bytes` is the true on-disk file size supplied by
the caller; `reassemble.rs` uses it only to compute the truncation
notice — it never recalculates it.

content.description:
Truncated file content, capped at 65 536 bytes by `reassemble.rs`.

Content is embedded inline in the fencepost, meaning that many large
included files will proportionally bloat `history.json` and per-turn
provider serialization. A future optimization should move large file
bodies to content-addressable storage keyed by their xxHash64 digest,
storing only the hash here and lazy-loading on demand. For now, the
65 536-byte per-file cap limits the worst-case size.

IncludedImageEntry.description:
An image file whose bytes are re-attached after compaction when the file
is flagged as important. Parallel to `IncludedFileEntry` but carries raw
bytes instead of UTF-8 text.

InterrogativeId.description: Identifier for a single interrogative (agent question) within a session.

last_activity_at.description:
Wall-clock timestamp of the last provider chunk, tool-call dispatch,
tool result, or agent-loop iteration for a subagent. Absent for
non-subagent jobs or jobs that have never started streaming.

stalled.description:
Whether a running subagent has been idle beyond the stall threshold
(wall-clock). Always false for non-subagent and non-running jobs.

oneOf.description: HTTP 400: the request omitted the `version` query parameter.
HTTP 400: the `version` query parameter is present but malformed.

HTTP 404: the opaque artifact ID is unknown in the current daemon
run and attached main session.

HTTP 409: the version token is well-formed but the snapshot is
stale, mismatched, or cannot be reproduced exactly.
HTTP 413: the artifact exceeds the maximum allowed size.
HTTP 500: an I/O failure prevented retrieval of the artifact.

KnownFeedbackArtifactError.description:
A recognized feedback artifact error. The `"type"` field identifies the
error and each kind corresponds to a specific HTTP status code.

oneOf.description:
The artifact is available for retrieval.

An available entry may carry an artifact kind the client does not
recognize (a kind introduced after this client was compiled). The
entry is still retrievable because the retrieval ID and snapshot token
are present. When no pinned content type is known for the kind, the
client skips content-type validation and accepts whatever content type
the daemon returns. The client should still display the entry and offer
retrieval; it must not reject the entry solely because the kind is
unrecognized.
The artifact is not available for retrieval.

KnownFeedbackArtifactManifestEntry.description:
A recognized manifest entry shape. The `"availability"` field selects
between available and unavailable.

kind.description:
Whether this user message was typed by a human or automatically
injected by the Goal Driver continuation system. Absent in legacy
history means a normal human-authored message.

oneOf.description:
Persisted display content for expanded client rehydration. Stripped
by `filter_history_for_provider` and never sent to providers.

allOf.description:
Projection of `Message::ContextCleared`: the non-destructive
context-clear fencepost appended on a `handoff_plan` new-context
approval. `plan_path` is `Option<String>` on the wire (the `Message`
variant carries `Option<PathBuf>`; the daemon converts via
`to_string_lossy` at projection). Because the field is already
`String`, the `#[schema(value_type=...)]`/`#[schemars(with=...)]`
annotations the `PathBuf` message variant needs are not required here.

oneOf.description:
Projection of `Message::ContextCleared`: the non-destructive
context-clear fencepost appended on a `handoff_plan` new-context
approval. `plan_path` is `Option<String>` on the wire (the `Message`
variant carries `Option<PathBuf>`; the daemon converts via
`to_string_lossy` at projection). Because the field is already
`String`, the `#[schema(value_type=...)]`/`#[schemars(with=...)]`
annotations the `PathBuf` message variant needs are not required here.

LockSource.description:
Records why the session's edit-format lock was acquired.

`Initial` means the lock was captured from the active model's `edit_format`
on the first turn of the session. `PostCompaction` means the lock was
re-acquired after a compaction fencepost cleared the previous lock.
`ModelSwitch` means the lock was updated because the user switched models
to a different edit format. This source is used for both clean swaps
(old tools unused) and retained swaps (old tools retained alongside new).

McpServerStatus.description:
Snapshot of a session's mutable state at a point in time.

Connection status of a configured MCP server.

McpServerStatusEntry.description:
Status of a configured MCP server, for client display and slash-command
typeahead.

McpTransportKind.description:
Transport mechanism for an MCP server connection. Distinct from
`TransportKind` in `error.rs`, which classifies provider HTTP error modes.

oneOf.description:
Fencepost recording a runtime model swap performed via `POST /model`.
Has no `prompt_id` because model switches happen outside any turn.
`filter_history_for_provider` strips this before history reaches any
provider adapter; replayed at startup by `replay_active_model` to
restore `AppState.active_model`.

Fencepost inserted when the daemon intentionally clears provider
context while keeping the UI session alive.

Daemon-injected notification batch drained from the per-session
notification queue. Has no `prompt_id` because it is opportunistic
daemon context, not a user request.

Fencepost inserted after compaction. Providers receive only the
fencepost and subsequent messages (see
`filter_history_for_provider`); prior history is summarized in
`summary` and re-attached structured state lives in `reattachment`.

Typed projection metadata persisted alongside `continuation_prompt`
so subsequent compactions can rebuild the earlier spine without
reparsing the canonical string. Backward-compatible: old payloads
without this field deserialize to `None`.

compaction_prompt.description:
The exact compaction system prompt (directive) that was sent to the
provider to produce this fencepost's summary. Stored for backward
compatibility with sessions created by the prior implementation.
NOT rendered in the TUI card or injected as continuation context
for new fenceposts that carry a `continuation_prompt`.

continuation_prompt.description:
The canonical post-compaction continuation prompt injected into the
continuing model and displayed verbatim in the TUI card. Contains
a short summary, earlier-user spine, recent conversation projection,
and structural reattachment — all XML-escaped and deterministically
assembled by the compaction pipeline. Backward-compatible: old
payloads without this field deserialize to `None` (legacy path).

oneOf.description:
Provider-visible reminder carrying tool-exposure context. Not bound
to a specific prompt.

Daemon-owned provider-visible reminder. Providers render this as
user-role context and own the final wrapper format.

Daemon-only audit record for an autonomous permission classifier
decision. This is projected to `/history` for human debugging, but
stripped before provider calls so the classifier's judgment cannot
affect subsequent model context.

Image file reference resolved from a user `@`-reference. Raw image
bytes are stored base64-encoded in the session log. Provider adapters
serialize this into their native image-content format.

MessageUserKind.description:
Identifies whether a user-shaped message came from the human operator or
from daemon-owned reiteration (Goal Driver continuation or parent-sent
subagent input).

ModelConflictResponse.description:
Possible 409 bodies from `POST /model`.

`turn_in_flight` and `no_change` use the standard [`ErrorBody`], while
`edit_format_locked` carries the two normalized formats and an operator
resolution hint.

ModelLocator.description: A model addressed directly by provider and model identifier.

provider_name.description: Model identifier Polytoken sends to the provider.

ModelRequest.description:
Body of `POST /model` requests. The `model` field is matched against
`ModelConfig.name` (the registry map key in `Config.models`); unknown
names produce a 400 `unknown_model` error.

Notification.description:
A queued notification. Drained into `Message::Notification` at the start of
the next `/prompt` turn.

NotificationAutodrainResponse.description:
Body returned by `GET /notification-autodrain` and successful
`POST /notification-autodrain` requests.

NotificationId.description: Identifier for a single notification in the per-session notification queue.

oneOf.description:
Catch-all for forward-compatible deserialization via `#[serde(other)]`.
Must be a unit variant — serde requires it for internally-tagged enums
with `#[serde(other)]`.

**Field-loss caveat:** if a future `NotificationType` variant carries
struct fields, those fields are silently discarded when the variant is
deserialized by an older binary that does not yet know about it. Callers
that need access to those fields must match on the concrete variant
before falling through to `Unknown`. If full field preservation becomes
necessary, promote this to a `serde_json::Value`-bearing variant (at
the cost of breaking the `#[serde(other)]` shorthand and requiring a
manual `Deserialize` impl).

NotificationType.description:
The kind of notification. Tagged enum with a forward-compat `Unknown`
catch-all so older clients/daemons deserialize future variants cleanly.

PendingTurnInputId.description:
Identifier for one daemon-accepted pending input submission while an agent
turn is already running.

PermissionMonitor.description:
Runtime permission-monitor mode.

The enum is represented as a tagged object on daemon HTTP and event wires
so callers can inspect runtime monitor state without reconstructing
variant-specific fields. Config stores the default monitor as
`PermissionMatcherKind` plus top-level autonomous settings.

PermissionMonitorResponse.description:
Body returned by `GET /permission-monitor` and successful
`POST /permission-monitor` requests.

PlanHandoffContext.description:
Structured payload attached to a `PlanHandoff` interrogative. The
presentation strings are carried on the event so non-TUI clients can render
the same review surface without reconstructing daemon-local state.

PreUserPromptDenied.description: Body of the 422 response from `POST /prompt` when a pre-user-prompt hook denies the turn.

oneOf.description: Assistant narrative text, preserved verbatim and in order.

A tool call rendered at its original position with a concise target
description and final status. Tool-result bodies are never included.

target.description: Bounded, redacted argument/target summary (e.g. a file path or query).

oneOf.description:
A harness-owned notice (system reminder, notification) at its
chronological position, distinctly labeled so it is not
misattributed as human or assistant content.

ProjectedItem.description: A single ordered fragment within a projected turn.

ProjectedToolStatus.description: Status outcome of a projected tool call.

ProjectedTurn.description:
A logical turn beginning with a user message and including all assistant
narrative, tool calls, and results before the next user message.

PromptAccepted.description:
Body of the 202 Accepted response from `POST /prompt`.

The daemon responds immediately with the freshly-minted `PromptId`
and the session it belongs to; the actual model output streams
asynchronously via `/events`.

oneOf.description:
When `Some`, the prompt was queued for the active turn instead of
starting a new turn. The daemon sets this when the turn slot is held.

PromptId.description:
Identifier for a single prompt (user turn) inside a session.

A session can process many prompts sequentially; each `DaemonEvent`
describing model output (`ContentBlockStart`, `ContentBlockDelta`,
`ContentBlockStop`, `MessageStart`, `MessageComplete`, `ModelError`)
carries the `PromptId` it belongs to so subscribers that connect
mid-turn can tell which frames cohere.

PromptRequest.description:
Body of `POST /prompt` requests.

Layer-1 minimum: a single text field. Future revisions may accept
structured `Message` content; the `#[non_exhaustive]`-adjacent
approach is to add optional fields rather than changing the shape.
Path registration itself is Task N's responsibility — this type
lives here so schema-stability checks pass now.

`max_tool_turns` is a per-request override for the agent-loop
iteration cap. `None` means "use the daemon-config value, falling
back to the built-in default". Zero is treated as unset.

source_detail.description:
Preserved source-chain detail from the underlying transport error
(e.g. reqwest decode error, hyper incomplete message, io EOF).
Populated only for `TransportKind::Other` and `TransportKind::Timeout`
/ `TransportKind::StreamInterrupted` where the source chain adds
diagnostic value. Never carries content or prompt data.

ProviderError.description:
Serialized failure modes that a model provider can report.

Lives in `polytoken-core` — and is therefore serde-serializable and
schema-emitting — because it is carried by `DaemonEvent::ModelError`
over the SSE wire. `Transport` carries a stringified `message`
rather than a live `reqwest::Error` so `polytoken-core` stays
I/O-free and the type remains `Clone + Serialize`.

`retry_after_seconds: Option<i64>` intentionally uses a plain
integer-seconds encoding rather than `chrono::Duration`. `chrono`'s
`Duration` type has no default serde impl and the Task E mandate
requires `Serialize`/`Deserialize`; integer seconds round-trip
cleanly across any JSON decoder and keep the type no-I/O.

ProviderErrorPhase.description:
Provider-wire phase where a provider error originated.

`LocalPreSendGuard` is intentionally included even though it is not an
upstream phase: the daemon can synthesize `ContextTooLarge` before making a
request when local threshold checks determine that no compaction escape hatch
exists.

ProviderUpstreamErrorMetadata.description: Sanitized upstream/provider error metadata safe to carry over daemon events.

ProviderUsageSnapshot.description: Raw usage numbers from the provider for observability.

boxed_until.description: Optional provider-supplied low-priority or degraded cooldown timestamp, serialized as RFC3339 text if present.

request_utilization_bps.description: Request-window utilization as basis points, from 0 to 10000, when the provider reports a finite request window.

ReasoningEffort.description:
Provider-facing reasoning-effort label selected for one runtime turn.

Configured model capabilities decide which labels are valid. The value stays
string-backed because provider families use model-specific label sets.

ReattachmentState.description:
Post-compaction reattachment payload. The orchestrator (Task F)
assembles this from the pre-compaction session state; the fencepost
carries it verbatim into history.

tail_messages.description:
Recent messages retained after compaction by the prior implementation.
New fenceposts leave this empty — the canonical `continuation_prompt`
is the sole source of recent context. Backward-compatible: old
payloads without this field deserialize to an empty `Vec`.
Legacy provider expansion still injects these when no
`continuation_prompt` is present.

ReloadResponse.description:
Body of `POST /reload` responses. `failed` lists the subsystems whose
reload step raised an error; partial failure does not roll back successful
subsystems. An empty `failed` vec means every subsystem reloaded cleanly.

extensions_changed.description:
Whether the extensions subsystem detected a content change. Defaults
to `false` for older-server compatibility (pre-T1c bodies omit the
field entirely; deserializers parse them with `extensions_changed:
false`).

mcp_servers_changed.description:
Whether the MCP servers subsystem detected a content change.
Defaults to `false` for older-server compatibility.

permission_monitor_changed.description:
Whether the active permission monitor or its protected-path inputs
changed during reload. Defaults to `false` for older-server
compatibility.

skills_changed.description:
Whether the skill registry detected a content change. Defaults to
`false` for older-server compatibility.

subagents_changed.description:
Whether the subagent registry detected a content change. Defaults to
`false` for older-server compatibility; reload detection is wired by
the daemon registry layer, so older bodies omit this field entirely.

ReloadSubsystem.description:
Identifies a subsystem whose reload step failed. The enum is non-exhaustive
so that adding a new reload target is not a breaking wire change; consumers
matching on this must include a wildcard arm.

RewindAccepted.description: Body of the 202 Accepted response from `POST /rewind`.

ScratchPad.description:
Identifies which scratch pad a [`StateDelta::ScratchWrite`] or
[`StateDelta::ScratchClear`] targets.

- `Session`: persists for the entire session lifetime, survives compaction
  and `/clear`. Replayed via the ungated catch-all in `replay_state`.
- `Context`: cleared on compaction or `/clear` (same lifecycle as the
  context window). Replayed with `barrier_index` gating.

credential_file_path.description:
Path to the daemon credential file. `None` for legacy records that
predate bearer auth (PT-235), and for non-daemonized launch paths
(exec mode, doctor) that bypass `run_foreground`.

model.description:
The active model registry name at session start. `None` for
pre-upgrade `record.json` files that predate this field. Some older
records may contain provider wire IDs from before TASK-195.

non_interactive.description:
Exec-mode marker for sessions started without interactive operator
affordances. Older registry records default to interactive mode.

session_title.description:
Operator-visible session title. Cosmetic metadata only; older registry
records default to `polytoken`.

SessionStateDomain.description:
Coarse invalidation domain for fields returned by `GET /state`.

The wire representation is a transparent string so future daemons can add
domains without making older clients classify `session_state_changed` as a
malformed known event. Clients should ignore domains they do not understand.

SessionStateSnapshot.description:
`plugin_config` accepts any JSON value and is trusted input;
no schema enforcement is applied at this layer. `PartialEq` is
derived (`serde_json::Value: PartialEq`) but `Eq` is intentionally
omitted because `serde_json::Value` is not `Eq`.

adventurous_handoff_active.description:
Computed value: `adventurous_handoff` flag is set AND the active facet
exposes `handoff_plan`. Defaults to `false` for older clients.

available_models.description:
All models available in this session, including dynamic provider models
discovered at startup or on `/reload`. The TUI uses this to populate
the `@model:` typeahead so it always reflects the daemon's resolved
config rather than a stale client-side snapshot. Empty for older daemons
that do not emit the field.

oneOf.description:
The active Goal Driver goal for this session, or absent when no goal is
set. A cleared goal is represented by absence, not a distinct lifecycle
state.

mcp_servers.description: Configured MCP servers and their current connection status.

symlink_warnings.description:
Symlinked config/context files skipped during the most recent config
discovery. Empty when no symlinks were encountered or when
`daemon.follow_symlinks_for_configs` is enabled.

turn_in_flight.description:
Whether a turn is currently running in this session. Use this as the
authoritative signal for whether prompt input should be locked, rather
than inferring it from conversation history.

SessionTitleRequest.description:
Body of `POST /title` requests.

An empty or whitespace-only `title` clears the operator override and
reverts the effective title to the inferred title (or the default when
no inferred title exists). A non-empty value sets the override, which
takes precedence over any inferred title.

SessionTitleResponse.description:
Body of `POST /title` responses.

`title` is the effective title after the request was applied (override
wins, else inferred, else the source-control-derived default). `overridden`
is `true` when an operator override is active and `false` when the
effective title comes from the inferred title or the default.

overridden.description: Whether an operator override is currently active.

title.description: The effective title after applying the request.

SourceControlSnapshot.description: Best-effort source-control identity for UI/status consumers.

ahead.description:
Number of commits on the local branch that are not on its tracked
upstream branch. Absent when no upstream is configured or the count is
unavailable.

behind.description:
Number of commits on the tracked upstream branch that are not on the
local branch. Absent when no upstream is configured or the count is
unavailable.

dirty.description:
Whether the working tree has uncommitted changes. Absent when the
status is unknown or the information is unavailable (for example, when
the source-control tool does not support dirty detection).

emitted_at.description: Wall-clock publish time. Not authoritative for ordering.

seq.description:
Monotonic per-daemon sequence. `None` only for subscriber-
synthesized protocol events (`StreamDiscontinuity`).

session_id.description: Session this envelope belongs to. Moved from per-variant payloads.

oneOf.description:
Persists the session-level edit-format lock.

Written once at the start of the first turn (source: Initial) and
once after a compaction fencepost clears the lock (source: PostCompaction).
Replayed by `session_state::replay_state` to restore `SessionState.edit_format`.

Persist the set of retained edit formats whose tools are still registered
because they were used earlier in the conversation. Replaces the entire
retained set. Emitted when a model switch retains the old format's tools.
Replayed barrier-gated (cleared across `CompactionFencepost` and
`ContextCleared`, same as `SessionEditFormatLocked`).

Write a key-value pair to a scratch pad.

Enforcement of key length (256 bytes) and value size (64 KiB
serialized) happens at the WRITE SITE before the delta is emitted,
not in `apply_delta_to_state` or `replay_state` (which are infallible).

Clear all entries in a scratch pad.

Not emitted as a persisted delta in the current plan — context scratch
is cleared via live-state mutation in `reset_context_scoped_fields` and
the compaction orchestrator. This variant exists for future hook use
(hooks writing to scratch pads may need an explicit clear path).

Persist a change to the active goal's metadata so it survives compaction
and `/clear`. This is a whole-goal snapshot replace: the daemon fold does
`state.current_goal = goal.clone()`. Replayed ungated like todos/flags
(NOT `barrier_index`/`context_clear_index` gated), so goal metadata is
durable session-scoped state that survives both barriers. The optional
`goal` field depends on the transition: `Some` for transitions that
produce or update an active goal, `None` for proposal, rejection, and
clearing.

Push a directory onto the session cwd stack (`pushd` tool).

`path` is an already-resolved, absolute, in-project path. Replayed
gated by `context_clear_index` (like `FileTouched`), so cwd survives
compaction but resets to the floor on `/clear`.

Pop the top of the session cwd stack (`popd` tool).

Replayed gated by `context_clear_index`, same as `Pushd`.

Records the active plan file path when `write_plan` writes a new plan.

Persisted in durable history and replayed by
`session_state::replay_active_plan_path` to restore the plan pointer
across daemon restart/session resume. The backward history scan
returns the latest `ActivePlanSet` or `ContextCleared`, whichever is
closer to the end, so context clears (which emit
`ContextCleared { plan_path: None }`) correctly override earlier
plan writes.

SymlinkWarningInfo.description:
Information about a symlinked config/context file that was skipped during
daemon config discovery. Surfaced to the TUI as a local-only warning card.

description.description:
Human-readable description of what was skipped (e.g. "AGENTS.md context
file", "skill directory").

path.description: The display path of the symlinked file or directory.

SystemReminder.description:
Daemon-owned reminder context that is provider-visible but hidden from the
TUI unless the operator opts in.

oneOf.description:
Re-fired after the working directory changed (a `pushd` or `popd`
relocated the top of the cwd stack).
The current working directory no longer exists on the filesystem.

An MCP server was disabled mid-session. Its tools remain in the
registry but calls will error. The model should stop calling them.
An MCP server was re-enabled mid-session. Its tools are usable again.

A permission rule with a `message` field was the resolved verdict for
a tool call. The `tool_name` identifies which tool triggered the rule.

No longer emitted by the agent loop as of PT-287 — the daemon now
injects a `Message::User` continuation instead. Kept for forward-compat
(serialized data may still contain it).

Queued notifications were auto-drained into the session history.
The reminder body tells the model these are harness-originated, not
user instructions.

The user returned to plan mode after working in another facet.
Stale todos from the execute phase should be reviewed and cleaned up.

TerminalReason.description: The reason a goal reached a terminal state, with optional detail.

detail.description: Optional human-readable detail about the terminal reason.

TerminalReasonKind.description: The category of reason a goal reached a terminal state. Known values (open set; other strings are forward-compatible): completed, blocked, abandoned.

TerminateStatus.description:
Terminate-response status discriminator.

Typed enum so future variants (`Draining`, `Terminated`) become
compile-time decisions on every consumer, rather than silent string
drift against a stringly-typed wire field.

TitleChangeSource.description:
How a session title change originated. Clients use this to surface
automatic inferences with a one-time hint, while operator `/title`
changes are already confirmed by the client that issued them.

TodoSnapshot.description:
Snapshot of a single todo entry captured at compaction time. Core-level
mirror of the daemon's richer `Todo` type, carried inside
`ReattachmentState` so post-compaction turns see the current todo list
without replaying `StateDelta` history.

emitted_at.description:
Timestamp of the StateUpdate that created this todo. Legacy snapshots
serialized before this field existed deserialize with the Unix epoch.

oneOf.description:
Transport-layer error during an extension network request (connection
refused, DNS failure, TLS error, etc.). Distinct from
[`ToolError::NetworkTimeout`] so callers can retry transient failures
differently from connectivity failures.

network_error.description:
Transport-layer error during an extension network request (connection
refused, DNS failure, TLS error, etc.). Distinct from
[`ToolError::NetworkTimeout`] so callers can retry transient failures
differently from connectivity failures.

oneOf.description: The extension network request exceeded the per-request timeout.

An unexpected internal host error occurred (e.g. a poisoned mutex).
Used by SDK host functions to propagate infrastructure failures back to
the guest as structured errors rather than panicking the daemon.

internal_error.description:
An unexpected internal host error occurred (e.g. a poisoned mutex).
Used by SDK host functions to propagate infrastructure failures back to
the guest as structured errors rather than panicking the daemon.

oneOf.description:
An MCP server is not reachable or has not yet connected. `state`
is a human-readable phrase such as `"disconnected: connection refused"`.

mcp_server_unavailable.description:
An MCP server is not reachable or has not yet connected. `state`
is a human-readable phrase such as `"disconnected: connection refused"`.

oneOf.description:
Emitted after compaction clears the session's edit-format lock and the
next turn re-locks to a different format. `from` and `to` are the
pre- and post-compaction edit-format strings (e.g. `"search_replace"`
and `"hashline"`).

ToolLoading.description: Controls when the model can see the available tools.

oneOf.description:
Persisted display content for expanded client rehydration. This is the
bounded version (from `ToolOutput.live_display`) persisted to durable
history so the TUI can rehydrate `DiffPreview` rendering after history
reloads. Stripped by `filter_history_for_provider` and never sent to
providers.

TransportKind.description:
Transport-layer classification for a `ProviderError::Transport`.

Coarse-grained on purpose: the daemon's retry logic cares about
broad categories (timeout-like vs refused vs TLS vs stream-interrupted
vs other) rather than fine-grained `reqwest` error kinds. Unit-variant
enum so it serializes as a bare JSON string.

TuiAttachmentLeaseId.description: Identifier for one daemon-minted interactive TUI attachment lease.

TuiAttachmentSnapshot.description: Public snapshot of the currently active interactive TUI attachment.

oneOf.description:
Token-usage snapshot from a provider stream.

Anthropic emits two `Usage` chunks per turn: one at `message_start`
(carrying `input_tokens`, with `output_tokens = 0`) and one at
`message_delta` (carrying `output_tokens`, with `input_tokens = 0`).
OpenAI emits a single `Usage` chunk at `response.completed` with
both counts populated. The daemon accumulates across chunks rather
than replacing, so the post-turn snapshot reflects the totals.

response_id.description:
Upstream response identifier (e.g. OpenAI `response.id`).
Populated by providers that echo a per-response id on the
terminal usage event; `None` for providers without the concept.

UnauthorizedResponse.description:
Body of a 401 Unauthorized response from the auth middleware.

Returned when the request omits a valid `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
header matching the daemon's startup credential. The `code` field is
always `"unauthorized"`; clients should treat it as a terminal signal
that the presented credentials were rejected (not a transient error).

message.description:
Human-readable explanation of why authentication failed. Never
includes the token, the header value, or any decoded bytes.

oneOf.description: Proceed with the request immediately.
Wait the specified duration before proceeding.
Do not proceed; treat like a rate-limit backoff.

UsageAction.description: A provider's recommendation about whether to throttle the next request.

VersionResponse.description:
Body of `GET /version`.

Returns the daemon's build version.

can_disable.description: Whether the model can turn reasoning off.

default_level.description:
Default reasoning effort when you do not name one. Must be one of
`levels` when present.

effort_set.description:
Effort family the levels belong to (for example an OpenAI
reasoning effort set).

levels.description: Discrete effort levels the model accepts, in provider order.

can_disable.description: Whether the model can turn thinking off.

WireModelReasoningCapability.description:
Reasoning capability metadata for a model, expressed as a wire type.

This mirrors `polytoken_config::ModelReasoningCapability` but lives in the
core vocabulary crate so the daemon and TUI can exchange it without a
core-to-config dependency. Conversion impls live in `polytoken-config`.
